front_matter.title: Master Outline Zero — What the Christian Life New Testament Can Do for You
front_matter.text:
What the Christian Life New Testament Can Do for You

The Christian Life New Testament was designed to assist the believer in spiritual growth and practical service. It can fill a need in the life of the average Christian and change his or her life-style.

From guilty to not guilty.
From death to life.
From darkness to light.
From hatred to love.
From weakness to power.
From bondage to freedom.
From tribulation to triumph.
From grief to joy.
From gloom to glory.
From defeat to victory.
From failure to success.
From fear to faith.
From I can’t to I can.

To get the most out of your Christian Life New Testament begin each study session with prayer. Ask the Holy Spirit to be your teacher and fill you with His power and give you a knowledge of His Word as you study. Remember that the Holy Spirit is the author of the Bible. “For prophecy never came by the will of man, but holy men of God spoke as they were moved by the Holy Spirit” (2 Pet. 1:21).

Do not rush through these Master Outline studies. They were prepared to be pondered over. Read them over and over; read them slowly and thoughtfully. Take time to look up each scripture reference and examine its contents that you may grasp what the Holy Spirit is teaching. Ask yourself, “How can this scripture apply to me?” Know that “all Scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness, that the man of God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work” (2 Tim. 3:16, 17). All Scripture is profitable to all believers in one way or another. Some scriptures will lead you to repentance; others can fill you with joy. Some scriptures will reveal the will of God, while others will put you under conviction of sin. Some scriptures will tell you of the love of God. Other scriptures will speak of His wrath.

Let me give you eight good reasons why you should study the Master Outlines in this New Testament.

(1) Study for a biblical foundation on which to grow.
(2) Study for spiritual strength and power for this life in a world under the curse of sin.
(3) Study that you may grow in Bible knowledge.
(4) Study that you may be a success to the glory of God.
(5) Study and give the Holy Spirit the opportunity to motivate you to greater things for the Lord.
(6) Study that you may know God’s perfect will for your life.
(7) Study that you may be an effective soul winner.
(8) Study so that you may “sanctify [set apart] the Lord God in your hearts, and always be ready to give a defense to everyone who asks you a reason for the hope that is in you, with meekness and fear” (1 Pet. 3:15).

When you fail to study God’s Word you stop growing. When you cease to grow spiritually you start deteriorating immediately. When you stop climbing you start slipping. You can never arrive spiritually in this life; there is always a higher plateau to be reached.

One of those plateaus is personal evangelism. The Christian Life New Testament can help you to reach this plateau. Jesus said, “Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men” (Matt. 4:19). Soul winners are made, not born. Master Outline Number Fifteen is a mini-syllabus on New Testament evangelism. It can help you to become a spiritual fisherman, because:

(1) It is small enough for the lady’s handbag and the man’s pocket.
(2) It is with you when you need it for witnessing or counseling.
(3) The Master Outlines and notes on the great doctrines of the Bible are so simple that anyone can understand the profound teachings of Jesus.
(4) It can give you confidence to share your faith with the lost.
(5) It will help you to answer some of the doctrinal questions you may be asked when discipling the lost for salvation. Let me give you a few examples from personal experience.

1. You may be asked to prove that the Bible is the Word of God. Never say that you can prove anything; you will only end up in an argument. Say something like this: “I will be glad to tell you why I believe the Bible is the Word of God.” Now turn to Point Number One, “THE BIBLE CLAIMS TO BE THE INSPIRED WORD OF GOD.” Read Second Timothy 3:16, 17 and the note I(A) on inspiration.

Now read Point Number Two, “THE BIBLE IS A DIFFICULT BOOK.” Read First Corinthians 2:14–16 and the note II(A) on difficulties.

Then turn to Point Number Three, “THE BIBLE IS A BOOK OF ONENESS.” Read Second Peter 1:21 and the note III(A) on the unity of the Bible.

Now give your personal experience of salvation—How you are now a new creature in Christ, the old things are passed away, and all things are new. Then say something like this: “This is why I believe the Bible is God’s Word.” Above all, trust the Holy Spirit to convict of sin.

2. You may be asked to prove the existence of God. Again, I caution you, do not try to prove anything. Say, “I will be happy to show you why I believe in the existence of God.” Then read Hebrews 11:5, 6 and the note I(A) on the existence of God. Again, trust the Holy Spirit to use His Word.

3. You may be asked to explain the Trinity of God. Read Matthew 3:16, 17 and the note V(A).

4. You may be asked to prove the Godhead of Jesus. Read John 1:1 and the note I(A) for the scriptural evidence of His deity.

When you become acquainted with the Christian Life New Testament, you will be able to answer some of the doctrinal questions you may be asked while sharing your faith or teaching a class. You will share your faith with some who will have spiritual hang-ups. You will need to help them with their doctrinal problems before you can lead them through “GOD’S PLAN OF SALVATION” and invite them to accept Christ as their personal Savior.

Years ago as I sat in my study meditating on Proverbs 23:7, I felt inspired to make a few simple notes. Now when things go wrong and I get down in the dumps I read “As a Man Thinks.” I have read it hundreds of times and it always motivates me to press on for my Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

Here it is:

To help overcome fear born of an inferior feeling and develop a positive mental attitude, read “As a Man Thinks” every day until it becomes a vital part of your daily thinking, motivating a change in your life-style from fear to faith. Remember, God said, “As he thinks in his heart, so is he” (Prov. 23:7).

AS A MAN THINKS

Today I will think like a dynamic servant of God, because I am what I think.

I am not always what I think I am; I am what I think.

I am not what I eat; I am what I think.

Clothes do not make the man; thinking makes the man.

Therefore, I will keep my thought processes active and open to the voice of God.

God did not call me to a life of failure, but to a life of success. This being so, I cannot fail as long as I do His will, allowing Him to work in and through me, motivating my every thought.

Because my God is a big God, I will think big with confidence, knowing my thoughts can never be bigger than my God.

Today I will think like the apostle Paul when he said: “I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me” (Phil. 4:13).

The Christian Life New Testament will help you mature spiritually. “To be carnally [sensuously] minded is death, but to be spiritually minded is life and peace” (Rom. 8:6). Tell me how you think and I will tell you whether you are a carnal Christian or a spiritual Christian. Remember, you are what you think.

I challenge you to compare your spirituality with that of the early Christians.

(1) They were accused of:
  a. Filling Jerusalem with the gospel. (See Acts 5:28.)
  b. Turning the world upside down. (See Acts 17:6.)

When they shared the gospel the people acted or reacted. On the day of Pentecost the hundred and twenty Spirit-filled believers left the upper room with the gospel. And as they shared it with the people, the people were confounded, amazed, and marveled. Some mocked and some inquired, asking, “Men and brethren, what shall we do?” (See Acts 2.) The point I wish to make is this: Some acted, accepting Christ as personal Savior, while others reacted, mocking. BUT NO ONE IGNORED THOSE HOLY SPIRIT-FILLED CHRISTIANS.

They were spiritual because they had a knowledge of the gospel and the filling of the Holy Spirit. They were thinking like the dynamic Christians they were. Now do you have the courage to ask yourself, Am I carnal or spiritual?

(2) Evidence of a Spirit-filled believer according to the New Testament:
  They were bold to share the gospel with the lost.
  They witnessed with great power.
  They shared with great grace.
  They shared their treasure, talent, and time.
  They worshipped in the Spirit.
  They suffered persecution and gloried in tribulations.
  They sang in prison, and loved and prayed for their executioners.
  They rejoiced to suffer shame for Jesus.
  They went everywhere proclaiming the gospel.

(3) Now let us look at a few characteristics of spiritual Christians:
  They do not care who gets the credit as long as God gets the glory.
  They do not have chips on their shoulders, but they do take up their crosses daily and follow Jesus.
  They ignore molehills and by faith move mountains.
  They have the ability to adjust without compromising principles.
  They can adapt to a changing world without letting the world change them.
  The question is, Am I a spiritual Christian? Only you can answer that question.

Here are some of the things you can do for your Lord and Savior Jesus Christ using the Christian Life New Testament.

(1) You can disciple the lost for salvation, person to person. Master Outline Number Fifteen, “HOW TO WITNESS EFFECTIVELY,” will teach you how to present Master Outline Number Fourteen, “GOD’S PLAN OF SALVATION.”

(2) You can disciple the lost for salvation by having a home Bible study for unsaved relatives, friends, and acquaintances. Have enough Christian Life New Testaments to loan one to each one present. Choose a mature Christian to lead the class—a teacher who will guide the discussion and get the class to participate. You will rejoice over the results.

(3) You can disciple the young believer for service on a one-to-one basis, or you can have a home Bible class, study the fifteen Master Outlines and watch these new Christians grow in the grace and knowledge of Christ.

(4) If you have an opportunity to share with a backslider, take him through Master Outlines, “THE ABUNDANT LIFE,” and “REPENTANCE.”

The Christian Life New Testament is great for:
  Family devotions,
  Memorizing scriptures,
  Personal Bible study and devotions,
  Giving as a gift to the saved or unsaved.

My prayer is that you will commit your all to the Lord Jesus Christ and take this tool and GO WITH THE GOSPEL.

Porter Barrington
Evangelist

front_matter.title: How to Use the Outline
front_matter.text:
THE CHRISTIAN LIFE STUDY OUTLINES AND NOTES

The Christian Life Master Outlines and Notes are the amplification of a ministry of over thirty-five years, both in the pastorate and in the field of teaching and evangelism. These lessons by Porter Barrington on the great doctrines of the Bible are simple without being ordinary, short without being shallow, brief without being dwarfed, positive without being stilted, and comprehensive without being complicated.

They were produced to fill a need in the life of the average Christian, to provide an incentive to know more of God’s Holy Word. If diligently studied, they will help to establish you in the faith and give you spiritual confidence.

It is suggested that you study the Master Outlines in the order given: one each day for fifteen days, and at the end of fifteen days, you will know more about the New Testament than you ever thought possible in such a short time. This study is equal to an advanced college course in Systematic Theology. If you review these lessons often, you will continue to grow in the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

To begin your study of the Bible with the Christian Life Outlines and Notes, turn to the pages following this introduction. Here you will find the fifteen MASTER OUTLINES on the great doctrines of the New Testament. It is suggested that you follow them in the order given, you take time to read each Scripture reference found in the notes.

To illustrate the MASTER OUTLINE system, we begin with MASTER OUTLINE NUMBER ONE: THE BIBLE—THE WORD OF GOD. You will find the introduction followed by five points. After reading the introduction, begin your study with point number I as follows:

I. THE BIBLE CLAIMS TO BE THE INSPIRED WORD OF GOD (Now turn to 2 Tim. 3:16, 17.)

After reading 2 Tim. 3:16, 17, you will see the capital letter A, preceding verse sixteen, and another capital letter A below the chapter, followed by an explanation of that Scripture under point number I.

At the bottom of the note it reads, “Now turn to 1 Cor. 2:14-16,” for point number II: THE BIBLE IS A DIFFICULT BOOK. In this manner, each point is linked with the next until you conclude with the last point in MASTER OUTLINE NUMBER FOURTEEN.

MASTER OUTLINE NUMBER FIFTEEN should be studied as a guide to witnessing, after the believer is “grounded in the faith.” Do not neglect this important opportunity for Christians to effectively share your faith.

Now look at the MASTER OUTLINES and begin your quest for the abundant Christian life.

CHRISTIAN LIFE STUDY OUTLINES

outlines.title: The Bible—The Word of God
outlines.summary:
MASTER OUTLINE NUMBER ONE
The Bible—The Word of God

It is so important for a young Christian to start right; therefore, the first lesson is designed to help establish your faith in the Bible, for it is the Word of God.

Keep in mind that the Bible is not a book of philosophy, although it is philosophical. Do not go to the Bible for a scientific treatise. However, there is no discrepancy between ascertained facts of science and the Bible. The Bible is not a book of history, but is found to be accurate when recording history. The Bible was given to man from God, revealing Jesus Christ, the Son of God, and God the Son, the only Savior (John 14:6). He is the center and the circumference. It is Christ from Genesis to Revelation (John 5:39).

The Bible is as high above all other books as the heavens are above the earth. Someone has said of the Bible: “Read it to be wise, believe it to be safe, and practice it to be right.”

  I. THE BIBLE CLAIMS TO BE THE INSPIRED WORD OF GOD
     (Now turn to 2 Tim. 3:16, 17.)
 II. THE BIBLE IS A DIFFICULT BOOK
     (Now turn to 1 Cor. 2:14-16.)
III. THE BIBLE IS A BOOK OF ONENESS
     (Now turn to 2 Pet. 1:21.)
 IV. THE BIBLE CLAIMS SPECIAL POWER
     (Now turn to Heb. 4:12.)
  V. THE BIBLE COMMANDS THE BELIEVER TO STUDY THE SCRIPTURES
     (Now turn to 2 Tim. 2:15.)

runs.v: The Bible is a difficult book because it came from the infinite to the finite—from the unlimited, all powerful God, to limited man. Therefore, you cannot understand the Bible as you would understand the writings of Plato or Socrates. You can study the great philosophers with the natural mind, and by diligent application, grasp their profound meanings. If the Bible could be understood by natural man, it would be a natural book, and could not be the Word of God. Since the Bible is from God, and therefore spiritual, before you can receive its teachings, you must be born of the Spirit (
) and filled with the Spirit (
). Always approach the Bible praying that the Spirit will be your teacher and will guide you to a better understanding of His Holy Word; or it will remain a difficult, closed book (

transition.raw: Now turn to 2 Pet. 1:21, for point number III: THE BIBLE IS A BOOK OF ONENESS.
transition.next_title: THE BIBLE IS A BOOK OF ONENESS

runs.v: The oneness or unity of the Bible is a miracle. It is a library of 66 books, written by over 35 different authors, in a period of approximately 1,500 years. Represented in the authors is a cross section of humanity, educated and uneducated, including kings, fishermen, public officials, farmers, teachers, and physicians. Included in the subjects are religion, history, law, science, poetry, drama, biography, and prophecy. Yet its various parts are as harmoniously united as the parts that make up the human body.

For 35 authors, with such varied backgrounds, to write on so many subjects over a period of approximately 1,500 years in absolute harmony, is a mathematical impossibility. It could not happen! Then how do we account for the Bible? The only adequate explanation is: “Holy men of God spoke
as they were
moved by the Holy Spirit” (verse 21).

You must also keep in mind that the Word of God contains the WORDs of God, as well as the words of Satan, demons, angels, and man—both good and bad. God is truth and cannot lie. Satan “is a liar and the father of it” (
). Man is natural and is therefore limited and does not always speak the truth. To illustrate:

. In this portion of Scripture, we have the words of Jesus, of the Pharisees, of the Herodians, and of the Sadducees. The Pharisees, Herodians, and Sadducees were trying to entangle Jesus in His teachings, that they might accuse Him of breaking God’s law. Their words were spoken with evil intent, revealing the thinking of the natural man, along with the words of God that came from the lips of Jesus.
As you study the Bible, ask yourself these questions:
Who is speaking: God, demon, angel, or man?
To whom is He speaking: to the nation Israel, to the Gentiles, to the Church, to men in general, or to some individual man or being?
How can this Scripture be applied to my own life to make me a better Christian?
Now turn to Master Study Outlines for lesson number two.

outlines.title: God
outlines.summary:
MASTER OUTLINE NUMBER TWO
God

The Bible reveals God as the only Infinite and Eternal Being, having no beginning and no ending. He is Creator and Sustainer of all things. He is the Supreme Personal Intelligence, and Righteous Ruler of His universe. He is life, and therefore, the only source of life (John 5:39).

Man is natural and cannot know God by wisdom. “Can you search out the deep things of God?” (Job 11:7 OT). God is a person and can be known only by revelation. In the Old Testament He revealed Himself to and through His prophets. In the New Testament He reveals Himself through His Son Jesus Christ (Heb. 1:1-3).

  I. THE EXISTENCE OF GOD
     (Now turn to Heb. 11:5, 6.)
 II. THE PERSONALITY OF GOD
     (Now turn to 1 Thess. 1:9.)
III. THE NATURE OF GOD
     (Now turn to 1 John 4:8.)
 IV. THE GRACE OF GOD
     (Now turn to Eph. 2:8, 9.)
  V. THE TRINITY OF GOD
     (Now turn to Matt. 3:16, 17.)

outlines.title: Jesus Christ—The Son of God
outlines.summary:
MASTER OUTLINE NUMBER THREE
Jesus Christ—The Son of God

Christianity differs from all religions, because it is more than a religion—it is the life of the Son of God made living in man. Christ is Christianity, and Christianity is Christ. He is the supreme subject of each book of the New Testament, and He fulfills all the promises of God in the Old Testament, from His incarnation to His Second Coming as “Lord of lords and King of kings” (Rev. 17:14). He is the God-man Christ Jesus in glory, exalted above all creatures, having “all authority ... in heaven and on earth” (Matt. 28:18).

During His earthly ministry, He claimed to be God incarnate (in human flesh). He is all that He claimed to be, or He is less than the least (Rev. 1:8). Before His claim can be denied, there are some things that must be accounted for:

His virgin birth;
His holy, sinless life;
His many miracles;
His vicarious death and His bodily resurrection.

  I. THE DEITY OF JESUS CHRIST
     (Now turn to John 1:1.)
 II. THE HUMANITY OF JESUS CHRIST
     (Now turn to Rom. 1:3, 4.)
III. THE VIRGIN BIRTH OF JESUS CHRIST
     (Now turn to Luke 1:26-35.)
 IV. THE DEATH OF JESUS CHRIST
     (Now turn to Phil. 2:8.)
  V. THE RESURRECTION OF JESUS CHRIST
     (Now turn to Matt. 28:1-20.)
 VI. THE ASCENSION AND SECOND COMING OF JESUS CHRIST
     (Now turn to Acts 1:9-11.)

outlines.title: The Holy Spirit
outlines.summary:
MASTER OUTLINE NUMBER FOUR
The Holy Spirit

The Holy Spirit is God, and is equal to the Father and the Son. Don’t ever speak of Him as “It” or refer to Him as “an influence.” He is God the Holy Spirit, and is set forth in the Bible as being distinct from the Father and the Son. In the Genesis account of creation, He is seen actively engaged in the work of creation, along with the Father and the Son. In the Old Testament, He came upon men to empower them for service; but, when they were disobedient, He departed from them.

When David sinned against the Lord, he prayed, “And do not take Your Holy Spirit from me” (Ps. 51:11 OT). In the New Testament, after Pentecost, we see the Holy Spirit indwelling the believer, never to leave him, filling and empowering him for service. The study of the person and work of the Holy Spirit is of utmost importance. A scriptural understanding of God the Holy Spirit will make you a better Christian and servant of God.

  I. THE DEITY OF THE HOLY SPIRIT
     (Now turn to Acts 5:3, 4.)
 II. THE EMBLEMS OF THE HOLY SPIRIT
     (Now turn to Luke 3:16.)
III. SINS AGAINST THE HOLY SPIRIT
     (Now turn to Matt. 12:31, 32.)
 IV. THE WORK OF THE HOLY SPIRIT
     (Now turn to John 16:7-14.)
  V. THE FRUIT OF THE HOLY SPIRIT
     (Now turn to Gal. 5:22, 23.)

outlines.title: Sin
outlines.summary:
MASTER OUTLINE NUMBER FIVE
Sin

In considering the question of sin, we are faced with two startling facts.

The first fact is that man makes so little of sin. To some, it is an illusion—a religious mirage—the invention of some fanatic. It is denied, joked about, and laughed at by man. Many who believe sin to be a fact continue in it with little thought of its penalty.

The second fact is that God makes so much of sin. God said, “The soul who sins shall die” (Ezek. 18:20 OT). “The wages of sin is death” (Rom. 6:23). All sins are an abomination to God (Prov. 6:16-19 OT), and He hates those who work iniquity (Ps. 5:5 OT). Moses said, “… All who behave unrighteously, are an abomination to the Lord your God” (Deut. 25:16 OT). Sin is an evil force. Its presence cannot be escaped in this life, but it can be overcome by the power of God.

  I. THE ORIGIN OF SIN
     (Now turn to Jude 1:6.)
 II. WHAT IS SIN?
     (Now turn to 1 John 3:4.)
III. HOW SIN ENTERED INTO THE WORLD
     (Now turn to Rom. 5:12.)
 IV. THE RESULTS OF SIN
     (Now turn to Eph. 2:1.)
  V. GOD’S REMEDY FOR SIN
     (Now turn to 2 Cor. 5:21.)

outlines.title: Judgments
outlines.summary:
MASTER OUTLINE NUMBER SIX
Judgments

In the Scriptures, we are instructed to “rightly [divide] the word of truth” (2 Tim. 2:15). This is most essential when studying the judgments. Do not endeavor to make all the judgments conform to the theory of one “general judgment.” The “general judgment” theory is the invention of religion and is not taught in the Word of God. There are five separate judgments revealed in the Bible, and they differ as to time, place, and purpose. Yet, they all have one thing in common: the Lord Jesus Christ is the judge (John 5:22).

Everyone—from Adam to the last man to be born on this earth—will stand before the Lord Jesus Christ to be judged.

In the first judgment, the sins of the believers have already been judged in Christ on the cross.

In the second judgment, the believer is to judge self, or be judged and disciplined by the Lord Jesus Christ.

In the third judgment, all believers must appear at the “judgment seat of Christ” where their works are to be judged.

In the fourth judgment, all nations are to be judged at the Second Coming of Christ.

In the fifth judgment, the wicked dead are to be judged at the great white throne.

  I. THE JUDGMENT OF THE BELIEVER’S SINS
     (Now turn to John 5:24.)
 II. THE JUDGMENT OF THE BELIEVER’S SELF
     (Now turn to 1 Cor. 11:31, 32.)
III. THE JUDGMENT OF THE BELIEVER’S WORKS
     (Now turn to 2 Cor. 5:10.)
 IV. THE JUDGMENT OF THE NATIONS
     (Now turn to Matt. 25:31-46.)
  V. THE JUDGMENT OF THE WICKED
     (Now turn to Rev. 20:11-15.)

outlines.title: Rewards
outlines.summary:
MASTER OUTLINE NUMBER SEVEN
Rewards

There is a vast difference in the doctrine of salvation for the lost, and the doctrine of rewards for the saved. Salvation is “the gift of God, not of works” (Eph. 2:8, 9). Salvation is received by faith in the Lord Jesus Christ (John 3:36). Rewards are according to the works of the believer (Matt. 16:27).

A most revealing Scripture concerning rewards is found on 1 Cor. 3:8-15. First, every believer will be rewarded “according to his own labor” (verse 8), not for labor for salvation.

Second, “we are God’s fellow workers” (verse 9)—not for salvation, but for rewards.

Third, the believer is to build on the Lord Jesus Christ, “for no other foundation can anyone lay than that which is laid, which is Jesus Christ” (verse 11).

Fourth, the believer has a choice of two kinds of building materials: “gold, silver, precious stones”—this is building with eternal materials; or “wood, hay, straw”—this is building with temporal materials (verse 12) (2 Cor. 4:18).

The believer who builds on Christ with eternal materials, “gold, silver, precious stones,” shall receive a reward. The works of “wood, hay, straw,” will be destroyed at the “judgment seat of Christ,” and the believer will suffer loss—not the loss of salvation, but the loss of eternal reward.

Some believers will be ashamed at the “judgment seat of Christ” (1 John 2:28)—ashamed of their works of “wood, hay, straw.”

In the first year of my ministry, I sat at the bedside of a dying friend. As we talked of his homegoing, tears filled his eyes. Being young in the Lord, I thought he was afraid to die, and attempted to speak words of encouragement to him. He said, “I am not afraid to die; I am ashamed to die.” He went on to say that Christ was his Savior, but he had lived for self, and now had to meet the Lord Jesus Christ empty-handed. His life loomed up before him as “wood, hay, straw.” He was “saved so as by fire.”

Rewards are called “crowns” in the New Testament.

  I. THE CROWN OF LIFE
     (Now turn to James 1:12.)
 II. THE CROWN IMPERISHABLE
     (Now turn to 1 Cor. 9:24-27.)
III. THE CROWN OF REJOICING
     (Now turn to 1 Thess. 2:19, 20.)
 IV. THE CROWN OF RIGHTEOUSNESS
     (Now turn to 2 Tim. 4:5-8.)
  V. THE CROWN OF GLORY
     (Now turn to 1 Pet. 5:2-4.)

outlines.title: The Church
outlines.summary:
MASTER OUTLINE NUMBER EIGHT
The Church

Jesus said, “I will build My church” (Gk. ecclesia) (Matt. 16:18). The word ecclesia in the New Testament is used to designate any assembly whether it be political (Acts 19:39), Christian (Eph. 1:22, 23), or national (Acts 7:38). It means a “called-out assembly” or “congregation.” God called Israel out of Egypt; they congregated in the wilderness; they were “the church in the wilderness.” Today, God calls the saved out of the world to congregate in worship. This is the church in the world, in it but not of it.

Unlike the church in the wilderness, the church that Jesus is building will never cease. He said, “The gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.” His church is not synonymous with Christendom. It is in Christendom in the same way in which it is in the world, in it but not of it. Christendom is made up of those who profess to be Christians, but they know not Christ as a personal Savior (Matt. 7:21-23, also, 2 Tim. 3:5 and Titus 1:16). Only blood-washed, born again, Spirit-baptized believers constitute the church that Jesus is building. It is called a:

(1) Mystery (Eph. 3:3-10).
(2) Body (1 Cor. 12:12-31).
(3) Building (Eph. 2:10-22).
(4) Bride (2 Cor. 11:2).

outlines.title: Prayer
outlines.summary:
MASTER OUTLINE NUMBER NINE
Prayer

Prayer is as old as man, as universal as religion, and as instinctive as breathing (Gen. 4:26 OT). It is practiced in some form by all men of all faiths. Prayer springs from the heart with a need—a need greater than man’s ability to encounter. Prayer is man’s acknowledgment of a being higher than himself.

Most men try to pray, yet so few know how. There are two kinds of prayers: the prayer that does not reach God and the prayer that does reach God. This is illustrated by our Lord in the parable of the Pharisee and the publican (Luke 18:9-14). Both men went to the same place, at the same time, for the same purpose—to pray.

The Pharisee prayed in his religious pride, expecting God to answer because he thought himself worthy. He informed God of his own goodness, that he was better than others. He boasted of his good works. He said, “I fast; I tithe.” This is the kind of prayer that does not reach God. It is self-righteous prayer.

Now look at the publican and his prayer. He came to God in great humility, conscious of his unworthiness, confessing himself a sinner, and begging for mercy. This is the kind of prayer that does reach God. This is righteous prayer.

It is a rare privilege to pray; because it brings you into close fellowship with God, admitting your need for Him and your utter dependence upon Him.

   I. WHAT IS PRAYER?
      (Now turn to Matt. 7:7-11.)
  II. WHY PRAY?
      (Now turn to Luke 18:1.)
 III. HOW TO PRAY
      (Now turn to Matt. 6:9-13.)
  IV. WHERE TO PRAY
      (Now turn to Acts 12:5.)
   V. HINDRANCES TO PRAYER
      (Now turn to 1 Pet. 3:7.)
  VI. DOES GOD ANSWER ALL PRAYERS?
      (Now turn to John 15:7.)

outlines.title: Faith
outlines.summary:
MASTER OUTLINE NUMBER TEN
Faith

“The just shall live by faith.” This declaration of the Christian’s principle of life is found four times in the Bible: Hab. 2:1-5 (OT); Rom. 1:17; Gal. 3:10, 11; and Heb. 10:38. In Habakkuk we see the difference between the lives of the unjust and the just. The unjust are puffed up and live by their own self-sufficiency. But the just live by faith—their confidence is in God. To them, faith is more than a philosophy of life; it is the very principle of life (Hab. 2:4 OT). The just shall live his whole life by faith. He is saved by faith (Acts 16:31); he is kept by faith (1 Pet. 1:5); and he lives by faith (Gal. 2:20). His faith shall be tried many times and in many ways (1 Pet. 1:7), but faith will always be vindicated, because it is more than equal to any occasion. Faith knows how to wait on the Lord (Is. 40:31 OT), and it is always victorious (1 John 5:4).

Faith defies reason; it moves mountains (Matt. 17:14-21). Faith does not view facts; it never gives up (Heb. 11:32-39). Faith says, “God is working out His perfect will by His will in my life, and I can wait, endure, and suffer.” Faith does not make anything easy, but it does make all things possible.

  I. WHAT IS FAITH?
     (Now turn to Heb. 11:1-3.)
 II. THE IMPORTANCE OF FAITH
     (Now turn to Eph. 6:16.)
III. LITTLE FAITH
     (Now turn to Matt. 14:28-33.)
 IV. THREE KINDS OF FAITH
     (Now turn to John 11:21-44.)
  V. THE HALL OF FAITH
     (Now turn to Heb. 11:32-39.)

outlines.title: The Abundant Life
outlines.summary:
MASTER OUTLINE NUMBER ELEVEN
The Abundant Life

“… I have come that they may have life, and that they may have it more abundantly” (John 10:10). The only way into eternal life is through faith in Christ as personal Savior (John 3:15). But do not stop here; to have eternal life is great—but there is more. Christ came that you might have life more abundantly. All believers have life, but not all have abundant life. You are living beneath your privilege if you are a believer and not enjoying the abundant life.

For life to be abundant, it must have abundant resources, and the only unlimited source of life is in the person Jesus Christ the Son of God (John 14:6). To possess this fuller life, the believer must abide in Him (John 15:1-5). Dynamic, abundant living is not for just a few—it is God’s norm for all believers. It is spiritual life in depth, and without it, the Christian life becomes inane and meaningless.

If you do not have abundant life within you, you will soon yield to the carnal (fleshly) life around you (1 Cor. 3:1-4). The carnal life is circumstance-controlled; the abundant life is Holy Spirit-controlled. The carnal Christian life leads to defeat; the abundant life leads to victory in Christ. Man seems to know everything about life except how to live it abundantly. From this moment on, determine not to be satisfied with anything less than God’s best: living life abundantly.

  I. THE ABUNDANT LIFE IS A YIELDED LIFE
     (Now turn to Rom. 6:10-13.)
 II. THE ABUNDANT LIFE IS A SERVICED LIFE
     (Now turn to Rom. 12:1, 2.)
III. THE ABUNDANT LIFE IS A SEPARATED LIFE
     (Now turn to Rom. 1:1.)
 IV. THE ABUNDANT LIFE IS A SPIRIT-FILLED LIFE
     (Now turn to Eph. 5:18-20.)
  V. THE ABUNDANT LIFE IS A MATURE LIFE
     (Now turn to 2 Pet. 3:18.)

outlines.title: Repentance
outlines.summary:
MASTER OUTLINE NUMBER TWELVE
Repentance

“He who covers his sins will not prosper, But whoever confesses and forsakes them will have mercy” (Prov. 28:13 OT).

God desires truth in the inward parts (Ps. 51:6 OT) and commands all men everywhere to repent (Acts 17:30). The sinner must repent before he can become the recipient of salvation by grace through faith (Eph. 2:8, 9). Someone said, “I repented before I understood the meaning of the word, but since then as a Christian I have repented many times.”

Repentance is the gift of God (Acts 5:31; also Acts 11:18). “The goodness of God leads you to repentance” (Rom. 2:4). The goodness of God is not merited; therefore, the result of His goodness, which is repentance, is a gift. The gift of repentance is an inward change produced by the convicting power of the Holy Spirit as the Word of God is proclaimed (Acts 2:37, 38; also John 16:7, 11). The results are “repentance toward God and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ” (Acts 20:21): faith that Christ died for our sins and that He was buried and that He rose from the dead (1 Cor. 15:1-4).

Repentance qualifies a man for salvation, but it takes faith in Christ to acquire it. True repentance is always coupled with faith. It is impossible to have saving faith and not repent. “Repentance toward God and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ” are essential and inseparable in salvation.

Faith without repentance is the ultimate of hypocrisy, and repentance without faith in the death, burial, and resurrection of Christ is sheer folly.

      (Now turn to 2 Pet. 3:9.)
  II. REPENTANCE PREACHED
      (Now turn to Mark 1:1-4.)

      (Now turn to Heb. 6:1.)
  IV. REPENTANCE AND GOD

outlines.title: The New Birth
outlines.summary:
MASTER OUTLINE NUMBER THIRTEEN
The New Birth

It is of the utmost importance that we have a clear understanding of what Jesus meant when, speaking with Nicodemus, He said, “You must be born again” (John 3:7). The new birth is a spiritual birth. It is as much a birth as the natural birth; it is not just a figure of speech. The first birth is of the “seed of man.” The second birth is of the “seed of God” (1 Pet. 1:23). Therefore, you cannot become a child of God by joining the church, any more than a monkey could become a man by joining the human race. He might act like a man, dress like a man, and try to live like a man—but he would still be a monkey. Now, if by some miracle, the monkey could be born again of the “seed of man,” then—and only then—could he become a man. The only way to become a child of God is to be “born again” (John 3:3), “not of corruptible seed but incorruptible, through the word of God which lives and abides forever.” This is the new birth.

The new birth is a new creation (2 Cor. 5:17).
The new birth is a spiritual resurrection (Eph. 2:1-9).
The new birth is regeneration (Titus 3:5).
The new birth is partaking of the divine nature of God (2 Pet. 1:4).
The new birth is receiving Jesus Christ as Savior and Lord, by faith (John 1:12).
The new birth is being made the “righteousness of God” (2 Cor. 5:21).

The new birth is compulsory if you are to become a child of God: “You MUST be born again” (John 3:7).

  I. JESUS AND THE TWO BIRTHS
     (Now turn to John 3:1-8.)
 II. THE NEW BIRTH ISSUES A NEW, SINLESS NATURE
     (Now turn to 1 John 3:9.)
III. THE NEW BIRTH IS INCORRUPTIBLE
     (Now turn to 1 Pet. 1:23.)

     (Now turn to John 3:14-18.)

     (Now turn to 1 John 5:1.)

outlines.title: God’s Plan of Salvation
outlines.summary:
MASTER OUTLINE NUMBER FOURTEEN
God’s Plan of Salvation

There are seven facts revealed in God’s plan of salvation, and as you study them, keep in mind that this is God’s plan—not man’s—it is God’s. There is no other plan that can save your lost soul and make you a child of God (Acts 4:12).

All roads may lead to Rome, but all religions do not lead to God and salvation. There is only one way, and that is God’s way; and God’s way is a person, and that person is His Son the Lord Jesus Christ (John 14:6).

God’s salvation is threefold: First, Christ appeared on this earth to save you from the penalty of sin, by putting away your sin by the sacrifice of Himself on the cross (Heb. 9:26). Second, He appeared in heaven, in the presence of God, after His resurrection, to save you from the power of sin (Heb. 9:24). Third, He will appear again on this earth, the second time, as “Lord of lords and King of kings” (Rev. 17:14) to save you from the very presence of sin (Heb. 9:28).

Now come to the seven facts of salvation with an open mind and a receptive heart. May God may bring salvation to your soul.

   I. IT IS A FACT THAT GOD LOVES YOU
      (Now turn to John 3:16.)
  II. IT IS A FACT THAT YOU ARE A SINNER
      (Now turn to Rom. 3:23.)
 III. IT IS A FACT THAT YOU ARE NOW DEAD IN SIN
      (Now turn to Rom. 6:23.)
  IV. IT IS A FACT THAT CHRIST DIED FOR YOU
      (Now turn to Rom. 5:6-8.)
   V. IT IS A FACT THAT YOU CAN BE SAVED BY FAITH IN THE LORD JESUS CHRIST
      (Now turn to Acts 16:30, 31.)
  VI. IT IS A FACT THAT YOU CAN BE SAVED AND KNOW IT
      (Now turn to 1 John 5:10-13.)
 VII. IT IS A FACT THAT GOD MAKES YOU A CHILD OF GOD AS YOU OBEY HIM
      (Now turn to Acts 5:29.)

outlines.title: How to Witness Effectively
outlines.summary:
MASTER OUTLINE NUMBER FIFTEEN
How to Witness Effectively

One day as Jesus walked by the sea of Galilee He saw two men, Simon, called Peter, and Andrew, his brother. They were fishermen. “And He said to them, ‘Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men’” (Matt. 4:19). Soul winners are made, not born. Therefore to be an effective witness, you must be taught, trained, and motivated by the power of the Holy Spirit.

Jesus took three years to teach and train His disciples in the art of soul winning. After His resurrection He instructed them to stay in Jerusalem and “wait for the Promise of the Father” (Acts 1:4-8). When the disciples asked Jesus if the time had come for Him to restore the kingdom of Israel, He answered, “It is not for you to know times or seasons which the Father has put in His own authority. But you shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you shall be witnesses to Me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.”

On the day of Pentecost, the hundred and twenty received power to witness; and any believer who will acquire the know-how can be an effective soul winner.

He can know that he and the Holy Spirit are a witnessing team. Peter said, “And we are His witnesses to these things, and so also is the Holy Spirit WHOM GOD HAS GIVEN TO THOSE WHO OBEY HIM” (Acts 5:32). Therefore, when you witness remember that “your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you” (1 Cor. 6:19, 20).

When you witness, trust the Holy Spirit to do three things:
(1) Illuminate the mind of the unbeliever.
All lost souls are in spiritual darkness (2 Cor. 4:3, 4).
(2) Stir the heart of the unbeliever.
As Peter preached Christ, the listeners were “cut to the heart” (Acts 2:37).
(3) Move the will of the unbeliever.
The prodigal returned home when he came to himself and said, “I will arise and go to my father” (Luke 15:18).

You may be up-to-date in all modern techniques of soul winning and able to quote the necessary Scriptures without a flaw; but if you do not evangelize in the power of the Holy Spirit, your soul winning efforts will be ineffective. Approach this Master Outline with an open heart and receptive mind, willing to be made fishers of men.
